INFY.NS.title: Kent coroner given 'limited information' on fatal Egypt boat fire
INFY.NS.summary: British man, Steven Hill, died in a boat fire off the coast of Egypt in June 2023, along with two other Britons who chose to stay in their rooms while the other 12 passengers went for an early morning dive. The cause of death could not be determined, but it is likely that prolonged exposure to heat and effects of the fire fumes led to Hill's death. The fire started due to a suspected electrical fault, but no official documentation was obtained regarding the incident.

INFY.NS.title: OpenAI offers free ChatGPT Go for one year to all users in India
INFY.NS.summary: OpenAI is offering its ChatGPT Go plan free of charge for one year to users in India starting November 4. The promotion is part of OpenAI's strategy to expand in one of its top markets, India with over 700 million smartphone users and over a billion internet subscribers. Existing ChatGPS Go subscribers will also be eligible for the free 12-month plan. The service, priced at less than $5 per month, launched in India in August and has since expanded to Indonesia and 16 additional countries across Asia. However, making money from ChatGpt's paid plans in India has been challenging, with the app generating only $3.6 million in in-app purchases during its 90 days leading up to August.

INFY.NS.title: Donald Trump ‘would love’ third term but rules out running for vice-president
INFY.NS.summary: Donald Trump has ruled out running for the vice-presidency in the 2028 US election, a proposal some of his supporters have suggested to allow him to serve a third term in the White House. However, he stated that he would not do this. The 22nd amendment of the US constitution prevents anyone from being elected to the presidency a third time. Some have suggested that if another candidate stood for president but then resigned, Trump could step up and assume the presidency again. The former US vice-president and Democratic presidential nominee, Kamala Harris, has also hinted at another run for president.

INFY.NS.title: Don’t believe everything you see: why Buddhist scepticism is vital in the age of generative AI
INFY.NS.summary: The latest iteration of OpenAI’s video generator, Sora 2, has introduced a new chapter of Buddhist scepticism, stating that objective reality is often obscured by prejudices and memories. The heart sutra, a key passage of Buddhist teachings, suggests that to overcome suffering, the five skandhas (skandhas) that make up human experience are empty. These include form, feelings, perceptions, and mental forces. The Venerable Miao Guang from the Fo Guang Shan monastery in Taiwan often demonstrated this, revealing that an image used by her often resembles a scoop of ice-cream, which is actually butter. The author argues that while Buddhism encourages scepticism of reality, it can only take a pessimistic point of view if it understands the lived experiences of many.

INFY.NS.title: Genocide: Trump describe killings for Nigeria as genocide, Tinubu reply - but wetin be genocide Pidgin
INFY.NS.summary: The United Nations Convention of Human Rights and Social Justice has been criticised for its limited definition of genocide. The ICJ, the highest judicial body, has been given power to settle disputes between states. The definition of the crime is defined as genocide, which can be defined by acts intended to destroy a national, ethnic, racial, or religious group. Since its adoption, various parties have argued that this definition is limited.

TM.title: Derbyshire Police warning to Toyota car owners after thefts
TM.summary: Police in Derbyshire have issued a warning to Toyota car owners to take extra precautions following a series of thefts. The incidents occurred between 2 October and 3 October, with 10 Toyota Rav 4 cars taken from addresses across the county. The police are currently investigating the incidents. Police are urging owners to keep their keys safe, particularly if their vehicles have keyless entry.

TM.title: Toyota denies promising $10bn investment in US after Trump announcement
TM.summary: The Japanese auto giant, Toyota Motor, has denied claims by US President Donald Trump that it is planning to invest over $10bn in the United States over the next few years. However, a senior executive at the company, Hiroyuki Ueda, stated that no such explicit promise of investment was made. The firm plans to continue investing and create new jobs in the US.

TM.title: Rob Burrow Centre for Motor Neurone Disease to open its doors
TM.summary: The Rob Burrow Centre for Motor Neurone Disease, a state-of-the-art facility dedicated entirely to MND care, research, education and holistic support, is set to open in Leeds later this year. The centre follows a £6.8m fundraising campaign led by Leeds Hospitals Charity and has been heavily supported by the community in Leeds, Leeds Rhinos and Kevin Sinfield. Rob's neurologist consultant at Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust, Dr Agam Jung, is the director for the centre. Building work has been completed less than 18 months after Rob's death.

TM.title: Corporation Bridge in Grimsby 'should stay shut until fixed'
TM.summary: The 100-year-old Corporation Bridge in Grimsby, North East Lincolnshire, has been recommended by councillors that it should remain fully closed until repairs are completed, with an estimated completion date of December 2023. The closure of the bridge has been delayed several times since it was scheduled to reopen before Christmas 2023, but it was later postponed until summer. The council fired its main contractor, Spencer Group, in May due to "unacceptable delays" and increased costs. The new contractor, Taziker, suggested keeping the bridge closed until the work is finished or reopening it with one lane and temporary traffic lights. A final decision on the bridge's future will be made at a cabinet meeting later.

TM.title: Men crash stolen taxi into parked and moving cars in Bideford
TM.summary: Police have arrested a man in his 30s after two men stole their taxi and drove it into parked and moving cars in Bideford, England. The men had been driven from Westward Ho! to a house where they promised payment and threatened the taxi driver. They then fled the scene and drove off at high speed, crashing into several parked cars and eventually involved in a crash with two other cars. The police have arrested the man and woman.

SPY.title: U.S. Futures, Global Markets Mixed After Fed Chair Dampens Further Rate Cut Hopes
SPY.summary:
The Federal Reserve has reduced interest rates, with Chair Jerome Powell expressing confidence in his ability to maintain the status quo. The S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average ended their four-day winning streak. The announcement of the reduced rates led to mixed reactions, with futures for both the S.P. and P.E.
.

SPY.title: Stock Market Today: U.S. Cuts China Tariffs After Trump, Xi Meet — Live Updates
SPY.summary: The U.S. is reducing its tariffs on China after President Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping met for the first time in six years. The move is seen as significant as a significant step forward in the future of the industry. However, stock futures remain steady as investors consider other developments.

SPY.title: Heard on the Street Friday Recap: Keep on Truckin’
SPY.summary: The news of a potential trade freeze led to a surge in stocks, with the S&P 500 gaining 0.8% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average adding 472 points. Despite President Trump's announcement of terminating trade talks with Canada, the stock market rallied, with strong consumer prices increasing by 3% from the previous year. Meanwhile, the Nasdaq Composite also rose by over 1.5%, with the rise of interest-rate cuts.

SPY.title: The Scott Trust board
SPY.summary: The Scott Trust aims to maintain the financial position and editorial independence of the Guardian in perpetuity. The Trust also promotes the causes of freedom of the press and liberal journalism both in Britain and elsewhere. Ole Jacob joined the trust in 2015 and was appointed as its Chair in 2021. Katharine Viner, the first female editor-in-chief of The Guardian, has been responsible for creating its reader revenue strategy and maintaining the website free to all. She also restored the Guardian’s finances, leading investigations, on-the-ground reporting on people and power, environmental journalism, culture, sport and multimedia. Tracy Corrigan is chair of the Scott Trust Endowment board and is a non-executive director of Barclays Bank UK PLC and Domino's Pizza Group PLC.

SPY.title: Jaguar Land Rover restart helps UK factories return to growth
SPY.summary: UK factories experienced a recovery in October after the reopening of Jaguar Land Rover operations and increased consumer spending. The S&P Global purchasing managers’ index (PMI) rose to a one-year high as business optimism improved and factory output expanded. The recovery was largely due to Jaguar's reopening facilities after a cyber-attack estimated to cost the UK economy £1.9bn. Consumers increased spending on new cars and industrial components, improving the outlook for industrial components. However, Mike Thornton, head of industrials at RSM UK, said it is uncertain if this is a temporary rebound in output rather than a sustained recovery. The UK's manufacturing sector has been hit hard by rising gas and electricity costs, rising wages and higher employment taxes since the pandemic.

AAPL.title: Apple is now worth $4,000,000,000,000
AAPL.summary: Apple has surpassed $4 trillion in market value, joining other companies such as Nvidia and Microsoft. Shares of Apple rose by 0.1% following strong iPhone 17 sales, a key market where the company has underperformed. This follows a period of decline in Apple's stock, which lost over $310 billion in one trading day in April. Despite this, Apple shares have only risen by over 7% this year. The record-breaking valuations have historically been Apple's.

AAPL.title: Apple Forecasts a Very iPhone Christmas
How Apple Skirted Disaster This Year
AAPL.summary: The world's largest retailer, Amazon.com, has seen a significant decline in its valuation and outlook for the future. The company has been criticized for its lack of transparency and for its handling of the situation. The world's most recent example of the Amazon.

AAPL.title: Apple claims 'tremendous' global uptake of latest iPhones
AAPL.summary: Apple's CEO, Tim Cook, stated that the latest iPhones have seen a "tremendous response" across the globe. The tech giant unveiled its thinnest iPhone and upgraded iPhone 17 models in September, and expects a strong Christmas and New Year period to be a success. However, Apple narrowly missed estimates for iPhone sales in its fourth quarter that ended in September due to supply constraints and a lag in shipments to China. Despite this, Cook stated that Apple is heading into the holiday season with "our most powerful lineup ever". The company also reported a $102.5bn in Q4, an 8% increase from the previous year, and projected sales to land between $206bn and $213bn for the current quarter through December.

AAPL.title: How Tim Cook Evaded Disaster at Apple This Year
AAPL.summary:
It took two quarters of the year for CEO Tim Cook to save Apple from a disastrous year. The company faced numerous challenges, including President Trump's tariffs, pending court ruling, and a lack of transparency regarding its relationship with the media.

.

TSLA.title: Elon Musk’s politics cost his firm Tesla more than one million EV sales, report reveals
TSLA.summary: A report by the National Bureau of Economic Research (Nebeth) has revealed that billionaire Elon Musk's political actions have significantly impacted Tesla's U.S. sales, costing the automaker billions in lost vehicle sales and benefiting rival electric carmakers. The study found that Tesla's sales would have been 67% to 83% higher, or about 1 million to 1.25 million additional vehicles, from October 2022 to April 2025, without the "partisan effect" of Musk’s political actions. The report also found that these actions negatively impacted California's progress towards its zero-emissions vehicle goals.

TSLA.title: Elon Musk wants you to know that Sam Altman got a refund for his Tesla Roadster
TSLA.summary: Elon Musk and Sam Altman, both of whom were founders at OpenAI, have been feuding on social media platforms X. Altman posted screenshots showing that he had reserved a Tesla Roadster in 2018 and tried to cancel it and request a refund on his $50,000 reservation fee, but his email bounced. Musk responded by saying that he received a refund within 24 hours and suggesting that the issue was resolved quickly. Both men have previously criticized each other, with Musk accusing Altman of stealing a nonprofit, a move he has previously made before in court and attempting to thwart OpenAI's attempts to restructure as a for-profit company.

TSLA.title: Associated Capital Group Inc. (41J.DE) Options - WSJ
Wall Street would rather be rich than right
TSLA.summary: The article discusses the hypocrisy of Wall Street in its trading, suggesting that everyone else would rather be rich than right. It suggests that the focus is on the "number go up" rather than the "business fundamentals". Examples include Tesla, a stock detached from its core business, where its core product, electric cars, is losing market share. However, Tesla is now an AI and robotics company, with its future being secured to robotaxis and $20,000 humanoid robots. The company's stock has risen 75% over the past 12 months and remains the world's most valuable car company with a $1.5 trillion market cap. Despite these controversies, Tesla's CEO, Elon Musk, who reportedly lost one million sales, remains the wealthiest person in the world and could become the first-ever trillionaire.

TSLA.title: Robotaxi companies must do more to prove safety, Waymo co-CEO says
TSLA.summary: Waymo co-CEO, Takedra Mawakana, has stated that other companies working on autonomous vehicles need to prove their technology is safe during an interview at TechCrunch Disrupt 2025. She cited that Waymo's vehicles are five times safer than human drivers and 12 times safer with respect to pedestrians. However, Tesla has not released any public data about the safety of its robotaxi pilot program in Austin, Texas.

BND.title: French Bond Yields Edge Up in Line With Market After Moody’s Lowers Outlook
BND.summary: French government bond yields have risen after Moody's Ratings lowered France's outlook to negative from stable due to concerns over its political instability and inability to address an elevated fiscal deficit and rising debt burden. The 10-year French OAT yield is up 0.5 basis point at 3.443%, according to Tradeweb. Meanwhile, Dutch government bonds have largely remained largely unaffected by the prospect of snap elections.

BND.title: Oakley Meta Vanguard review: fantastic AI running glasses linked to Garmin
BND.summary: The Oakley Meta Vanguard, a displayless AI glasses designed for running, cycling and action sports, have been reviewed for their deep Garmin and Strava integration. They are a replacement for running glasses, open-ear headphones, and a head-mounted action cam all in one. The Vanguard, priced at £499 ($499), are part of Meta's partnership with EssilorLuxottica, the owner of Ray-Ban, Oakley, and many other top brands. The design, fit and finish of the glasses are praised for their wraparound visor, arms, and three-point fit system. The central camera can capture 12-megapixel photos of reasonable quality and stabilised video up to 3K resolution for up to five minutes at a time. The glasses also feature a free link to the Meta AI app on your phone to interrogate your stats in real time.

BND.title: WTA Qatar Total Open - Scores & Schedule - Tennis
Stafford's Halloween house targets even bigger fundraising total
BND.summary: A family of Halloween enthusiasts, Elliot Smith and Tanya Quick, are aiming to raise over £2,000 for charity through their spooky-themed house in Stafford, England. The family has decorated the outside of the house, built a witch's hut extension and opened the garden gate for public visits. The donations can be made through the donation box on the front wall or by scanning the QR code on posters pinned to the gate. The money raised has been used to fund trips for up to 20 families affected by childhood cancers.

BND.title: Hampshire: Disabled parking fines total more than £380,000
BND.summary: Hampshire County Council has issued over £380,000 in fines for disabled parking, according to figures released through a Freedom of Information request. The increase reflects a significant expansion of the council's parking enforcement responsibilities, with 749 fines issued in 2020 and 5,418 in 2021. The county council has also taken over responsibility for on-street parking enforcement across the entire county. To combat blue badge misuse, enforcement teams conduct regular patrols across the county.

AGG.title: Meta Launches Jumbo Bond Sale; Stock Slides After Earnings
AGG.summary: The social media company, which is seeking to raise at least $25 billion through a six-part bond sale, has seen its shares fall by around 11% following a disappointing earnings report. Proceeds from the sale will be used for general corporate purposes, including increasing spending on artificial intelligence. The company's bonds also fell in demand, pushing the spread between the 5.4% bonds due in 2054 over U.S.

AGG.title: Kieran Bond given six life sentences for raping children
AGG.summary: Kieran Bond, a 33-year-old man from Bursledon, Hampshire, has been sentenced to six life sentences for sexually assaulting a boy and a girl under the age of 18. The offences were committed between 2018 and 2021. Bond will serve a minimum of 16 years before being considered for parole.

AGG.title: AI mania tanks CoreWeave’s Core Scientific acquisition; it buys Python notebook Marimo
AGG.summary: Core Scientific shareholders voted down an all-stock acquisition offer from competitor CoreWeave, which was valued at $9 billion. The vote was made following a vote-no recommendation from their largest shareholder, Sina Toussi of Two Seas Capital. The company's stock has surged since its IPO, rising from $14 billion to $66 billion as investors see it as a way to get involved in AI. However, Tousi argued that Core Scientific can turn into another CoreWeoway. Meanwhile, CoreWeaway acquired Python notebook Marimo for an undisclosed sum.

AGG.title: Maddeen and Loughmacrory: Title-winning clubs join forces to celebrate unique bond
AGG.summary: The two winning clubs, Madden and Loughmacrory, celebrated their first Armagh senior football title on Sunday during the county championship action. The victory was celebrated at the Athletic Grounds in Omagh, where another of the siblings, Ryan, was involved in LoughMacrory's victory over Trillick. The celebrations extended into the night, with the Madden team arriving into Loughmory for a combined title-winning party. The two teams had a significant impact on each other after losing their members in a road traffic accident in 2023.

AGG.title: Chicago father of child fighting cancer released on bond by immigration judge
AGG.summary: Chicago man Ruben Torres Maldonado, a 40-year-old painter and home renovator, has been released on bond by an immigration judge to return home after his deportation case went through the system. The judge cited Torres Maldanado's lack of criminal history as a reason for his release. His daughter, Ofelia Torres, 16, was diagnosed with a rare form of soft-tissue cancer in December and has been undergoing chemotherapy and radiation treatment. The Department of Homeland Security alleges that Torres Maldenado has been living illegally in the US for years and violates his due process rights. The arrest comes after weeks of tense encounters and aggressive tactics by federal immigration agents involved in Operation Midway Blitz.

GLD.title: Darlington trans row hospital trust 'feared bullying label'
GLD.summary: Eight nurses have brought a claim against County Durham and Darlington NHS Foundation Trust after a trans member of staff, Rose Henderson, was allowed to use the female changing room. Jane Shields, who worked at Darlington Memorial Hospital but is not one of the claimants, stated that about 80% of the female staff were unhappy about this arrangement. Kirsten Coutts, another nurse, expressed concern over the situation and was threatened with disciplinary action. The tribunal heard that the head of human resources, Andrew Thacker, did not mind that transgender patients are not allowed to be placed with biological women at any point during their hospital stay but were instead placed in a side room.

GLD.title: Angel Trust charity launches annual Christmas toy appeal
GLD.summary: The Angel Trust, a charity based in Bishop Auckland, has launched its fifth annual toy appeal to ensure every child in County Durham receives a Christmas gift. The appeal is seeking donations for all age groups, with over 12,500 items expected to be donated in 2024. The charity is also seeking make-up and skin-care gift sets for older children. All donations can be donated at the trust's Emporium shop at Perth.

GLD.title: Gold Rises on Likely Technical Recovery
GLD.summary:
The front-month Comex gold for October delivery fell 2.8% overnight, causing a significant increase in demand. However, Capital Economics’ John Higgins believes the price will ultimately fall further. Factors such as reserve managers’ diversification out of the dollar may continue to influence the price, but this may not be the case.
.

EEM.title: San Francisco mayor: 'We should be the testbed for emerging tech'
EEM.summary: San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie has stated that he believes that the city should be a testbed for emerging technology and AI, and all types of technology. He also expressed pride in the success of Waymo, an Alphabet-owned autonomous vehicle tech company, in the Bay Area. However, he acknowledged that safety comes first and that regulations for autonomous vehicles are regulated at the state level. While Lurie is open to autonomous vehicles, other cities like Boston may not be so cautious.

EEM.title: Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong trolls the prediction markets
EEM.summary: CoinCoinbase CEO Brian Armstrong made controversial remarks during the company's third quarter earnings call, where he inadvertently mentioned the words Bitcoin, Ethereum, Blockchain, Staking, and Web3, which were among the words users on "mention markets" on Kalshi and Polymarket had bet on these words being spoken on the call. While these words may have helped some users make money, they also highlighted the vulnerability of these markets to executives who become aware of them. A spokesperson for the company stated that it prohibits employees from participating in prediction markets or related activity around the company.

EEM.title: Argentinian Stocks Surge in U.S. After Milei's Election Win
EEM.summary: The victory of President Javier Gonzales' party in Argentina's midterm elections has led to a surge in shares in shares of Argentinian companies listed in the U.S. companies. Shares of oil-and-gifted company YPF and e-commerce platform MercadoLibre surged significantly, with shares of banks Banco Macro, BBVA Argentina, and Mercada.

SIE.DE.title: New York AG Letitia James challenges appointment of US attorney in Albany
SIE.DE.summary: New York Attorney General Letitia James has filed a motion to challenge the appointment of the US attorney for the Northern District of New York and quash a Justice Department subpoena related to a criminal investigation into her civil case against Donald Trump's finances. The motion was unsealed late Friday by Judge Lorna Schofield, who granted the attorney general's request to unseal the motion. This is the latest challenge to the appointment by a Trump administration pick for a US attorney position. Another challenge will be heard next month.

SIE.DE.title: The world’s most valuable public company just laid out its vision for the future
SIE.DE.summary: Nvidia, the world's most valuable public company, has outlined its vision for the future of its technology, aiming to make its chips crucial for artificial intelligence central to everyday life. The company's CEO, Jensen Huang, made his first keynote address at the GTC AI conference in Washington, DC. He emphasized the importance of AI technology in everyday life, with the company's focus on cell phone towers, robotic factories, and self-driving cars. Despite facing challenges such as competition from rival chipmakers AMD and Qualcomm, and trade restrictions, Nvidia is positioning itself as a significant player in a tech arms race spanning the globe. It is also releasing a blueprint for how other firms should build massive, “gigascale” AI data centers, or “AI factories,” which Oracle, Microsoft, Google, and other tech firms are investing billions in. Additionally, Nvidia announced a partnership with telecom firms T-Mobile and Nokia to build "AI-native” 6G cell phone tower, the next generation of wireless technology. It also plans to help build 100,000 self-autonomous cars in partnership with Uber using its chips and software, and is providing Palantir with computing power and AI models to help companies build AI agents and systems to automate processes. The firm's stock (NVDA) was up nearly 3% on Tuesday.

SIE.DE.title: ‘All will be forgiven’: Farmers and lawmakers have all eyes on Trump-Xi meeting with a bailout hanging in the balance
SIE.DE.summary: Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins has revealed that her team has found a legal way to unlock billions in relief funds for US farmers caught up in the trade war with China. The move involved tapping into a Depression-era fund and transferring leftover funds from the prior fiscal year to reopen all 2,100 USDA county offices by paying two employees per office to come back to work. This move unlocked over $3 billion in emergency aid and regular program assistance that had already been approved by Congress. However, it is unclear if farmers will also be helped with a larger relief package. The government shutdown has complicated the process, raising questions about whether a farm bailout will materialize. Some Trump officials believe that a larger bailout may not be necessary if a deal with Chinese leader Xi Jinping results in a lower tariff and a resolution of the trade dispute.

IGLS.L.title: Next PLC Lifts Outlook After Quarterly Sales Beat Guidance
IGLS.L.summary: U.S. fashion retailer Next has increased its outlook for the fiscal year after better-than-expected sales for the third quarter, with a 10.5% increase in total full-price sales compared to the previous year. The company is seen as a significant indicator of the future of the U.N.

IGLS.L.title: Associated Capital Group Inc. (41J.DE) Options - WSJ
Visit Jersey appoints group to deliver survey
IGLS.L.summary: Visit Jersey has appointed a research group to deliver the Visitor Exit Survey Programme from 2026 to 2028. The survey, which is based on the UK Office for National Statistics' International Passenger Survey, will provide "robust statistics" on volume, characteristics and experiences of island visitors. The TSE has previously delivered similar statistics for the Isle of Wight, and the Man.

IGLS.L.title: Renault Says Chinese Auto Group Geely Will Take 26.4% Stake in Brazilian Unit
IGLS.L.summary: Renault has announced a deal with Chinese auto group Geely to take a 26.4% stake in its Brazilian business. The deal allows Geely Holding Group and Geely Automobile Holdings to have access to the resources of the company and will allow them to produce Geely Auto branded vehicles alongside Renault vehicles at its Ayrton Senna manufacturing plant.

MSFT.title: Microsoft Sued by Australian Watchdog Over AI Pricing
MSFT.summary: The Australian government is suing Microsoft, alleging that the company misled its 2.7 million customers by making it difficult for them to pay for new artificial-intelligence services. The complaint alleges that Microsoft did not clearly explain how to opt out of paying for these services when their annual plans renewed.

MSFT.title: Microsoft Heads For $4 Trillion Market Cap
MSFT.summary: The rise of Microsoft's market value has put it on track to surpass $4 trillion for the first time. The company briefly traded above that level in July and August and first achieved it in January 2024. Both companies are set to report their quarterly earnings later this month.

MSFT.title: Microsoft Needs to Open Up More About Its OpenAI Dealings
MSFT.summary: The article discusses the lack of transparency regarding the company's relationship with OpenAI, suggesting that it will be difficult for the public to comprehend. The company's annual report revealed that it included the losses from its OpenAI stake in a $4.7 billion expense line for the fiscal year.

MSFT.title: Microsoft sued for allegedly misleading millions of Australians with its AI pricing
MSFT.summary: Microsoft has been sued by the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) for misleading millions of Australians about its office suite pricing increase. The ACCC alleges that the tech giant failed to disclose a third option of paying the same lower price and opting out of the AI, Copilot, in Microsoft 365 plans. This option was only revealed when subscribers began cancelling their subscription. The annual subscription price for the Microsoft 365 personal plan increased by 45% from $109 to $159 with Copilot included. The maximum penalty would be $50m.
